scenario.notes: IMPORTANT AGENT CONSTRAINTS: organize axes as a time-forward hierarchical tree matching the scenario; tree depth = time (root = earliest state, leaves = latest). Every non-root axis MUST declare its parent via gate — the parent's module becomes the gate, which both anchors tree parentage and scopes the signal to cells expressing the parent's program (the biologically correct behavior for both sub-states and sequential transitions). For sibling-vs-sibling discrimination at a branch point, pass the sibling modules as negatives on the same gated axis. Use a plain axis (no gate, no parent) ONLY for roots: scenario-given starting states (one or several, as the scenario allows), populations that do not progress within the window, terminal populations whose precursor isn't represented, and cycling/proliferating populations. Naming: <chainPrefix>_<descriptiveTail>; <chainPrefix> is one camelCase token (no underscores) grouping axes from the same lineage. When you gate across chains (parent has a different <chainPrefix>), the child MUST use a fresh, unique <chainPrefix> — reusing a prefix that already exists in a different subtree creates ambiguity. Cover the full cell landscape implied by the scenario; preserve continuous maturation gradients rather than treating states as discrete clusters.
